module_title: Commercial Banks and the Basics of NPA
introduction: At this beginner level, we will understand the basic business model of a commercial bank (how they actually make money) and define the biggest headache for the banking sector: The Non-Performing Asset (NPA).

core_concepts.title: Commercial Banks
core_concepts.description: These are profit-seeking financial institutions. Their primary function is to accept deposits from the public and lend that money to businesses and individuals in the form of loans. Examples: SBI, HDFC, ICICI, PNB.

core_concepts.title: The Banking Business Model (Spread)
core_concepts.description: Banks pay a lower interest rate to depositors (e.g., 4% on savings) and charge a higher interest rate to borrowers (e.g., 9% on a home loan). The difference between the lending rate and the deposit rate (here, 5%) is called the 'Spread'. This spread is the bank's core profit.

core_concepts.title: CASA Ratio
core_concepts.description: CASA stands for 'Current Account and Savings Account'. Banks pay zero interest on Current Accounts and very low interest on Savings Accounts. Therefore, CASA deposits are the cheapest source of funds for a bank. A higher CASA ratio means the bank is highly profitable.

core_concepts.title: NPA (Non-Performing Asset)
core_concepts.description: If the principal amount or the interest installment (EMI) of a loan remains unpaid for more than '90 days', the loan is officially classified as an NPA. In simple terms, it is a 'Bad Loan' that has stopped generating income for the bank.

important_entities.name: NPA Rules for Agriculture
important_entities.significance: Because agriculture depends on harvest seasons, the 90-day rule is scrapped. 1. For 'Short Duration Crops' (like wheat/rice): A loan becomes NPA if the installment is unpaid for 2 crop seasons. 2. For 'Long Duration Crops' (like sugarcane): It becomes NPA if unpaid for 1 crop season.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A classic exam trap. Remember: The money YOU deposit in the bank is the bank's 'Liability' (because they owe it back to you). The loan the bank gives out is the bank's 'Asset' (because it earns them interest). Therefore, a defaulted loan is a 'Non-Performing ASSET', not a liability.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The moment an EMI crosses the 90-day (3-month) mark past its due date, the banking software automatically tags it as an NPA.

exam_strategy_tips: The full form of CASA and its significance is an all-time favorite in banking and SSC exams. High CASA = Cheap Funds = High Profitability.
